page.layout: One page of running text in one column, numbered theses with Latin and Greek; no margin notes. Below the text: a rule, then the gathering signature at the right.

main_text.p: Vt merito olim prudentissimus Seneca, nisi Medi-cus venam contrectet, tuto mederi non posse tradi-derit. Seneca in Epistolis.
Therapeutica vero Medicinæ summa perfectio exsistit; cui etiam vel soli principatus palma iure co-tribuitur. Medendi methodum vocat Galenus.
Vtitur interim illa triū aliarum ancillantium ope-râ, quib. tota morborum curatio perficitur.
Illasque Medicinę partes vel solas Medicos olim cognouisse & exercuisse quoq;, certū est, easq; o-mnium esse vetustissimas. Hippocr. in lib. de Arte.
Diætâ omnes morbos esse curandos, non malè voluit Asclepiades. Apud Galenū in Lib.de tuend.san.
Pharmaca non, sed Naturam potius Morbos cura-re; Galenus. D.Lang.Epist.med,t.1.Ep.12.
Chirurgiam vero Medici præstantiam & laudem solam promereri, Aristoteles. In Problem sect.1.
main_text.head: EPILOGVS.
main_text.p: Adeoq; hæc sunt, quæ de hac Vniuersali Medicinæ-Constitutione, summa rerum capita excipere, eaque παχυλῶς ὡς ἐν τύπῳ Disputantib. disceptanda proponere volui.

page.notes: No page number, running head or catchword is printed. Numbered theses are kept as paragraphs. "XLIIX." is printed that way (sic). "Galenū" and "triū" are read with a macron or tilde; uncertain. The Greek in the epilogue ("παχυλῶς ὡς ἐν τύπῳ") is read from the scan. The signature Greek is uncertain. The "ę" in "Medicinę" is read as printed.
